fatal_errors: Al0.1CrCoFeNi is incorrectly described as equiatomic.

The cited evidence concerns deformation-induced chemical rearrangement in Al-Cr-Co-Fe-Ni and does not establish that this mechanism governs the thermal stability of sub-10 nm high-entropy nanoparticles.
No quantitative temperature, stress, particle-size, atmosphere, or exposure-time window is specified.
explanation: The response proposes a coherent, falsifiable alternative about stress-induced short-range ordering and includes useful no-load and tensile controls. The evidence supports competition between configurational entropy and pairwise enthalpy, and broadly supports deformation-induced rearrangement in Al0.1CrCoFeNi. However, it does not reconstruct the target AuCoCuNiPt nanoparticle system, vacuum-heating intervention, surface-energy-driven Au/Cu segregation, shape-dependent diffusion, evaporation, or particle-size loss. Its transfer from a deformation study to nanoalloy thermal stability is insufficiently justified, and XRD peak shifts or broadening are not uniquely diagnostic of chemical short-range order without element-sensitive diffuse scattering or atom-resolved compositional measurements. Thus it is experimentally testable but is a different, only partially supported mechanism rather than a reconstruction of the target.
